walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Geography: Fluvial & Coastal Environments — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Geography: Fluvial & Coastal Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Geography: Fluvial & Coastal Environments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between physical and economic water scarcity?
options: Physical scarcity is insufficient water supply for demand (e.g. arid regions); economic scarcity is inability to access available water due to lack of infrastructure or investment, despite water being present.
Hydraulic action is when the river dissolves rocks chemically.
Water scarcity only happens in dry countries.
Economic scarcity means water is too expensive for governments to buy.

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.
Economic scarcity means water is too expensive for governments to buy.
Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.

mcqs.q: What is hydraulic action in a river?
options: The force of moving water itself compressing air into cracks in the river bank or bed, weakening rock until pieces break off — no sediment needed.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Hydraulic action is when the river dissolves rocks chemically.
Hydraulic action is when rocks in the river smash into each other.
